Both letters address a Civil Aeronautics Board certification decision through the same machinery: presidential review of a proposed order, evaluation of whether traffic can support unsubsidized service, use of a temporary three-year certificate as a test of economic viability, and direction concerning the Board's order. C24 and C21 share the CAB review-and-reconsideration framework, but lack C04's distinctive combination of traffic viability, subsidy concerns, and a three-year test period.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"International local service should not, in general, be instituted in the absence of a reasonable probability that such service can survive.","parent_excerpt":"Renewing the certificates of both carriers for a limited period would afford them an equal opportunity to demonstrate their capacity to develop adequate traffic to operate without subsidy or to prove definitely that the route cannot economically support two carriers.","explanation":"Both make certification depend on demonstrated traffic and the route's ability to sustain economically viable service."},{"child_excerpt":"Can it be expected...that traffic on this route would expand sufficiently to satisfy the Board's present \"use-it-or-lose-it\" policy within the three-year duration proposed for this certificate? If so, does the Board find that the carrier's operations on this route could become self-supporting?","parent_excerpt":"Accordingly, I request the Board present' for my approval a revised order in this case which would certify both Northwest Airlines and Pan American World Airways...for a temporary period of three years from now.","explanation":"The shared three-year certification period functions as a test of whether traffic will develop enough for self-supporting operation."},{"child_excerpt":"there remains the necessity of judging whether the subsidies involved are or would become excessive","parent_excerpt":"it must not be wasteful duplication at the expense of the Federal Government...operate without subsidy","explanation":"Both center the presidential certification judgment on limiting federal subsidy exposure."},{"child_excerpt":"I am compelled to return the Board's proposed order without my approval.","parent_excerpt":"I request the Board...present for my approval a revised order in this case","explanation":"Both employ presidential return or revision of a CAB proposed order rather than merely offering general aviation policy commentary."}]}
